question.problem:
Find the eigenvectors of the $2\times 2$ matrix $C$ given that 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]C=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the matrix $[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]$ appears on both sides of the equation. Since this matrix is invertible (its determinant is not zero), left-multiplying the equation by the inverse gives the following expression for $C:$ 

$$
C={{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

Therefore, $C$ is diagonalizable. The eigenvalues of $C$ are ${\lambda }_{1}=-4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=6$ and the corresponding eigenvectors are the columns of the matrix $P.$ Computing $P,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}P={[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, the corresponding eigenvectors are: 

$\,$ ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
